# Owned recursive enum and interface key fixture

A generic interface keeps its class-owned Object key separate from the method's
recursive Enum<Self> formal. A default overload forwards a null fallback through
the inherited abstract contract. An opaque implementation checks dynamic receiver,
token, key and fallback identity, original effects, partial writes and exact late
failures. Four immutable caller routes run 96 fresh JVM cases twice in source and
SDK-contract profiles. Every recovered unit compiles with original class/method
metadata, and six wrong programs plus six Code-preserving metadata controls guard
the proof. Only owned fixture code executes. Use JDK 25; originals use release 8.
